```{r, include = FALSE}
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE

```

A hook is an R function that Deputy calls at a fixed point in a run: before a
tool runs, after it returns, when the run stops, and so on. Use hooks to log
what an agent does, keep an audit trail, block particular tool calls, or stop
a run early.

## Add a hook

Create a hook with `HookMatcher()`, naming the event and the callback, and add
it to an agent:

```{r}
library(deputy)

log_tool <- HookMatcher(
  event = "PostToolUse",
  callback = function(tool_name, tool_result, tool_error, context) {
    cli::cli_inform("{tool_name} finished")
    NULL
  }
)

agent <- Agent$new(
  chat = ellmer::chat("openai/gpt-6-luna"),
  tools = tools_file(),
  permissions = permissions_readonly()
)
agent$add_hook(log_tool)
```

For tool events, `pattern` is a regular expression that limits the hook to
matching tool names. `hook_matches()` tells you whether a hook applies to a
tool:

```{r, eval = TRUE}
library(deputy)

watch_writes <- HookMatcher(
  event = "PreToolUse",
  pattern = "^(write_file|edit_file|multi_edit)$",
  callback = function(tool_name, tool_input, context) {
    cli::cli_inform("{tool_name}: {tool_input$path}")
    NULL
  }
)
hook_matches(watch_writes, "edit_file")
hook_matches(watch_writes, "read_file")
```

## Events

| Event | Fires | Callback arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `PreToolUse` | before a tool runs | `tool_name, tool_input, context` |
| `PostToolUse` | after a tool returns | `tool_name, tool_result, tool_error, context` |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | after a tool fails | `tool_name, tool_result, tool_error, context` |
| `PostModelRequest` | after each model request of a run | `context` |
| `PermissionRequest` | when the permission policy denies a call | `tool_name, tool_input, permission_result, context` |
| `SessionStart` | at the start of each run | `context` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | at the start of each run, with the task | `prompt, context` |
| `Stop` | at each stop of a run | `reason, context` |
| `SessionEnd` | once, when the run has ended | `reason, context` |
| `SubagentStart` | when a subagent starts a delegated task | `agent_name, task, context` |
| `SubagentStop` | when a subagent finishes | `agent_name, task, result, context` |
| `PreCompact` | before older turns are summarised | `turns_to_compact, turns_to_keep, context` |
| `PostCompact` | after a summary is installed | `result, context` |
| `Notification` | when Deputy reports something, such as a denied call | `message, context` |
| `ConfigChange` | when `set_permission_mode()` changes the mode | `key, old_value, new_value, context` |

`context` is a named list with the working directory, the agent and run
identifiers, and fields specific to the event, such as the tool's annotations
for `PreToolUse` or the run's usage for `Stop`. `?HookEvent` lists them all.

`Stop` and `SessionEnd` also get the run's `ending` in `context`: a
`RunEnding` value that says whether the run was answered, stopped, hit a
limit, was cut off by the provider or failed. `PostModelRequest` gets the
run's usage so far, so you can show what a run is spending while it runs:

```{r}
agent$add_hook(HookMatcher(
  event = "PostModelRequest",
  callback = function(context) {
    cli::cli_alert_info(
      "Request {context$request_number}: {context$usage$total_tokens} tokens so far"
    )
    NULL
  }
))
```

## Block a tool call

A `PreToolUse` hook runs after the permission policy has allowed a call, and
can still deny it. Return `HookResultPreToolUse()`:

```{r}
no_secrets <- HookMatcher(
  event = "PreToolUse",
  pattern = "^write_file$",
  callback = function(tool_name, tool_input, context) {
    if (grepl("\\.env$|secrets", tool_input$path)) {
      return(HookResultPreToolUse("deny", reason = "Don't write to secret files."))
    }
    NULL
  }
)
agent$add_hook(no_secrets)
```

The model sees the reason and can try something else. A `PreToolUse` hook
can only take permissions away: calls the policy denies never reach it.

## Allow a denied call

A `PermissionRequest` hook runs only when the policy denies a call, and can
allow the call anyway. Use it to ask a person before running something the
policy would refuse:

```{r}
ask_before_code <- HookMatcher(
  event = "PermissionRequest",
  pattern = "^run_r_code$",
  callback = function(tool_name, tool_input, permission_result, context) {
    cat(tool_input$code, sep = "\n")
    if (isTRUE(utils::askYesNo("Run this R code?", default = FALSE))) {
      return(PermissionResultAllow())
    }
    NULL
  }
)
agent$add_hook(ask_before_code)
```

Returning `NULL` keeps the denial, and `PermissionResultDeny()` replaces its
reason. An allowed call runs with your R session's access, so treat this hook
as part of the permission policy.

## Stop a run from a hook

`PostToolUse` hooks see each tool's result or error. Return
`HookResultPostToolUse(continue = FALSE)` to end the run after the current
tool:

```{r}
stop_on_error <- HookMatcher(
  event = "PostToolUse",
  callback = function(tool_name, tool_result, tool_error, context) {
    if (!is.null(tool_error)) {
      cli::cli_alert_danger("{tool_name} failed: {tool_error}")
      return(HookResultPostToolUse(continue = FALSE, stop_reason = "tool_failed"))
    }
    NULL
  }
)
```

`HookResultPreToolUse()` also takes `continue` and `stop_reason`. Both take
`additional_context`, text that Deputy appends to the system prompt.

## Check an answer and send the run on

A `Stop` hook sees a run that has just stopped. Return `HookResultStop()` to
send an answered run on: Deputy asks the model again with your message, in the
same run, so the run keeps its ID, its limits and its usage, and a stream
carries on. This is how to check an answer and ask for a fix without starting
a second run:

```{r}
needs_sources <- HookMatcher(
  event = "Stop",
  callback = function(reason, context) {
    # Only an answered run, and only once.
    if (!S7::S7_inherits(context$ending, RunEndingAnswered)) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    if (context$stop_hook_active) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    answer <- agent$last_turn()@text
    if (!grepl("Sources:", answer, fixed = TRUE)) {
      return(HookResultStop("Add a 'Sources:' line listing what you read."))
    }
    NULL
  }
)
agent$add_hook(needs_sources)
```

`Stop` fires again when the run next stops, with `context$stop_hook_active`
set to `TRUE`. Check it, as the hook above does, or the hook can send the run
on for ever; the run's limits are the only other thing that would stop it.
`SessionEnd` fires once, when the run has really ended. Only an answered run
is sent on: a run that was stopped, hit a limit or failed ends as it stands.
The result's `response` is the text of the last pass, and its `turns` hold
them all.

## Wait for something

A callback can return a promise of its result. Deputy waits for it before
going on, so a hook can ask a person, call another model or read a file
without blocking your R session:

```{r}
ask_reviewer <- HookMatcher(
  event = "PreToolUse",
  pattern = "^run_bash$",
  promise_timeout = 300,
  callback = function(tool_name, tool_input, context) {
    # ask_someone() returns a promise that resolves to TRUE or FALSE.
    promises::then(ask_someone(tool_input$command), function(approved) {
      if (approved) NULL else HookResultPreToolUse("deny", reason = "Not approved.")
    })
  }
)
```

`promise_timeout` is how long Deputy waits, in seconds; the default is 60. A
promise that is rejected or hasn't settled by then counts as no answer and is
recorded as a hook error, and for `PreToolUse` that denies the call. Where the
wait happens depends on the event:

* `PreToolUse` and `PermissionRequest`: before the tool runs.
* `PostToolUse` and `PostToolUseFailure`: before the next model request. The
  tool's result is already recorded when the hook answers.
* `PostModelRequest`, `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `SubagentStart`,
  `SubagentStop`, and `PreCompact` and `PostCompact` during automatic
  compaction: before the run goes on.
* `Stop` and `SessionEnd`: before the run finishes. While a `Stop` hook waits,
  the agent is still running, so it refuses a new run until the hook answers.
* `Notification` and `ConfigChange`, and any hook fired by `$compact()`:
  Deputy doesn't wait.

If you call `agent$interrupt()` while a hook is waiting, the run stops when
the hook's promise settles: a tool that was waiting doesn't run, and a `Stop`
hook's answer no longer sends the run on. The same goes for a callback that
calls `agent$interrupt()` itself: the tool it was asked about doesn't run.
Otherwise a hook that returns a plain value behaves as it always has.

## Built-in hooks

`hook_log_tools()` prints a line after each tool call saying whether it
succeeded. `verbose = TRUE` adds a short preview of the result:

```{r}
agent$add_hook(hook_log_tools(verbose = TRUE))
```

`hook_block_dangerous_bash()` denies shell commands that match patterns such
as `rm -rf`, `sudo` and `chmod 777`. Add your own patterns with
`additional_patterns`:

```{r}
agent$add_hook(hook_block_dangerous_bash(
  additional_patterns = c("DROP\\s+TABLE", "TRUNCATE")
))
```

A pattern list catches accidents, not a determined adversary, so don't rely on
it to make `run_bash` safe.

`hook_limit_file_writes(dir)` denies writes and edits outside `dir`, applying
the same path rules as `Permissions(file_write = dir)`. Use it to add a second
check, or to confine writes more tightly for one agent than its policy does.

## Order and errors

Hooks for an event run in the order you added them, and the first hook that
returns something other than `NULL` decides; later hooks for that event don't
run. So return `NULL` from hooks that only observe, and add hooks that can deny
a call before hooks that might allow it. The built-in hooks return `NULL`
unless they deny a call.

If a `PreToolUse` hook throws an error, Deputy denies the tool call. An error
in any other hook is reported and the run carries on. A promise that is
rejected or times out is handled the same way. `agent$hooks$last_errors()`
lists recent hook errors.

## Run a hook in a separate process

Hooks run in your R session by default, so they can read and update your
objects. Give `HookMatcher()` a positive `timeout` (in seconds) to run the
callback in a fresh R process that is killed if it takes too long. That
process can't see your session's objects, so refer to package functions with
`::`, for example `deputy::HookResultPreToolUse()`. It can't return a promise
either.

## Hooks or results?

Hooks are for reacting while a run is in progress. To analyse a run afterwards,
use the `AgentResult` instead: `result_tool_calls()`, `result_tool_results()`
and `result$events` hold the same information, without any hook state to
manage, and `result$ending` says how the run ended. With `$stream_async()`,
`stream_result(stream)` gives a promise of that result.

[Human input and approvals](approvals.html) shows hooks that ask a person to
approve a tool call before it runs.
